claims.text: NOAA's Central Pacific Hurricane Center advisory (11 PM HST, 15 August 2026): Hurricane Lala had maximum sustained winds of 75 mph (120 km/h) and a minimum central pressure of 988 mb, located near latitude 19.6N, longitude 157.0W, about 65 miles west of Kailua-Kona and 130 miles south-southeast of Honolulu, moving northwest at 15 mph with gradual weakening expected Sunday. Forecast rainfall totals were 4-8 inches for the Big Island and windward Maui with a storm-total maximum of 30-35 inches over windward Hawaii Island, and 4-6 inches (maximum 8 inches) for the remaining islands, with 1-3 feet of storm surge; the advisory warned these amounts 'will produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of steep terrain.'

Emergency Proclamation Relating to Tropical Storm Lala, signed 14 August 2026 by C. Kimo Alameda, Ph.D., Mayor of the County of Hawaiʻi, under Hawaii Revised Statutes Chapter 127A, declaring a local state of emergency for Hawaiʻi County citing NWS forecasts of winds of 74-110 mph, rainfall of 8-12 inches (10-15 inches over windward areas), storm surge of 1-3 feet, and surf heights of 15-20 feet, with potential for 'considerable damage, downed trees and power lines, and power and communications disruptions.'

claims.source_name: Office of the Governor of Hawaiʻi
claims.text: Governor Josh Green signed a statewide emergency proclamation on 13 August 2026 ahead of Tropical Storm Lala, mobilizing state agency personnel, equipment and resources; the Hawaiʻi National Guard was prepared to support response efforts. A follow-up state update (16 August) reports approximately 180 Hawaiʻi National Guard personnel positioned statewide, including a 41-member Task Force Hawaiʻi and a 19-member Task Force Maui, and confirms the Hawaiʻi Department of Transportation closed Hilo International Airport (ITO) and Ellison Onizuka Kona International Airport (KOA) at 2 p.m., with Hawaiʻi Island and Maui County commercial ports also closed to all terminal, facility and vessel operations absent US Coast Guard approval.

GDACS tracked the storm as Central Pacific tropical cyclone ONE-C-26, active 12-16 August 2026, rating it a Green alert (low humanitarian impact) with maximum sustained winds of 130 km/h (Category 1), an estimated 10,000 people affected by Category 1 or higher wind speeds, a maximum storm surge of 0.2 m, and 'low' vulnerability assessed for the United States.

NOAA's Central Pacific Hurricane Center Advisory Number 20 (11 PM HST, 16 August 2026): Tropical Storm Lala located near 20.7N 162.6W, about 305 miles west of Honolulu and 225 miles west-southwest of Lihue, with maximum sustained winds of 60 mph (95 km/h) and a minimum central pressure of 997 mb, moving westward at 13 mph. 'There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.' Lala is forecast to become a hurricane again by Wednesday while continuing to move westward away from the main Hawaiian Islands.

County of Hawaiʻi update (posted 16 August 2026, 7:37 PM): all non-emergency County operations suspended Monday, 17 August, following Hurricane Lala's impact on the island; 'record-breaking' power outages reported (no specific figure given), multiple road closures documented on the County's Hazard Impact Map, 43 people sheltering at two emergency shelters (Nāʻālehu Elementary School and Robert N. Herkes Gym), search-and-rescue operations ongoing in Nāʻālehu, Waiʻōhinu and Pāhala, and an island-wide 'Essential Only' water-conservation request.

GDACS tropical cyclone report for ONE-C-26 (episode 20, reporting window 12 Aug 2026 15:00 UTC - 17 Aug 2026 09:00 UTC): overall Green alert (low humanitarian impact); maximum sustained winds 139 km/h (Category 1), up from 130 km/h in the prior report; affected population approximately 10,000 people in Category 1 or higher wind zones, unchanged.

County of Hawaiʻi flash-flooding update (16 August 2026, 1:07 AM): the County coordinated search-and-rescue operations in Nāʻālehu and Waiʻōhinu in Kaʻū after severe flash flooding cut off road access and inundated homes; National Guard high-water vehicles and a US Coast Guard helicopter assisted, and rescued residents were transported to Robert N. Herkes Gym in Pāhala and the Public Works base yard. Mayor Kimo Alameda: 'Our highest priority is the safety of our residents.'

description: Hurricane Lala strengthened to a Category 1 hurricane as it passed close to Hawaii Island on 15-16 August 2026, prompting a Hawaii County emergency proclamation (14 August, Mayor C. Kimo Alameda) and a statewide emergency proclamation (13 August, Governor Josh Green) ahead of the storm's approach. NOAA's Central Pacific Hurricane Center's 11 PM HST advisory on 15 August put Lala's maximum sustained winds at 75 mph with a central pressure of 988 mb, located about 65 miles west of Kailua-Kona and moving northwest at 15 mph, with forecast rainfall of up to 30-35 inches over windward Hawaii Island and warnings of life-threatening flash flooding and mudslides. A Hurricane Warning was in effect for Hawaii County and a Tropical Storm Warning for Maui, Oahu and Kauai counties. The State of Hawaiʻi activated approximately 180 National Guard personnel statewide, closed Hilo International Airport and Kona International Airport, and closed Hawaiʻi Island and Maui County commercial ports, while GDACS separately tracked the storm (as Central Pacific system ONE-C-26) as a Green/low-impact Category 1 system affecting an estimated 10,000 people. No death toll, injury count, or displacement figure has been confirmed via an allowlisted government or NOAA source as of this record. Re-checked 17 August 2026: Lala passed closest to Hawaii Island on 15-16 August, then weakened; NOAA's Central Pacific Hurricane Center Advisory 20 (11 PM HST, 16 August) put it as a tropical storm with 60 mph sustained winds and a 997 mb central pressure at 20.7N 162.6W (about 305 miles west of Honolulu), moving westward at 13 mph away from the main Hawaiian Islands, with no coastal watches or warnings in effect, though NOAA forecasts Lala could re-strengthen into a hurricane by Wednesday as it continues moving away. GDACS's tropical cyclone report (episode 20, window 12-17 August 2026) recorded a peak of 139 km/h sustained winds (up from 130 km/h) with the affected-population estimate unchanged at about 10,000. The County of Hawaiʻi's 16 August 7:37 PM update reports 'record-breaking' power outages (no county-published figure), multiple road closures, and 43 people sheltering at two emergency shelters (Nāʻālehu Elementary School and Robert N. Herkes Gym), with search-and-rescue operations ongoing in Nāʻālehu, Waiʻōhinu and Pāhala after flash flooding cut off road access in those communities on 16 August, and all non-emergency County operations suspended 17 August; an island-wide 'Essential Only' water-conservation notice was issued by the County Department of Water Supply due to storm-caused outages affecting water-system operations. No allowlisted government or NOAA source has published a confirmed death toll, injury count, quantified power-outage figure, or displacement total as of this re-check; unofficial media reports describe an unconfirmed storm-related fatality near South Point under investigation, but no allowlisted source was fetchable to verify it.

impact.summary: As of NOAA's 11 PM HST 15 August advisory, Lala was a Category 1 hurricane with 75 mph sustained winds and a 988 mb central pressure, about 65 miles west of Kailua-Kona and forecast to bring up to 30-35 inches of rain to windward Hawaii Island with life-threatening flash flooding and mudslide risk; a Hurricane Warning covered Hawaii County and a Tropical Storm Warning covered Maui, Oahu and Kauai counties. Hawaii County and the State of Hawaiʻi both issued emergency proclamations (14 and 13 August respectively) ahead of the storm's approach, and the state activated about 180 National Guard personnel, closed Hilo and Kona airports, and closed Hawaiʻi Island/Maui County commercial ports. No death toll, injury count, power-outage figure, or displacement total has been confirmed via an allowlisted government or NOAA source. Re-checked 17 August 2026: NOAA's Advisory 20 (11 PM HST, 16 August) shows Lala weakened to a tropical storm with 60 mph sustained winds, located about 305 miles west of Honolulu and moving away from the main Hawaiian Islands, with no coastal watches or warnings currently in effect (though NOAA forecasts possible re-strengthening to a hurricane by Wednesday). GDACS's updated tropical cyclone report recorded peak sustained winds of 139 km/h (up from 130 km/h), with the affected-population estimate unchanged at about 10,000. The County of Hawaiʻi's 16 August update (7:37 PM) reports 'record-breaking' power outages (no county-published number), multiple road closures, and 43 people sheltering at two emergency shelters, with search-and-rescue operations ongoing in Nāʻālehu, Waiʻōhinu and Pāhala after flash flooding cut off road access on 16 August, and all non-emergency County operations suspended 17 August; the County water department also issued an island-wide 'Essential Only' conservation notice due to storm-related power outages affecting water operations. No allowlisted government or NOAA source has yet published a confirmed death toll, injury count, quantified power-outage figure, or displacement total; unofficial media reports of an unconfirmed storm-related traffic fatality near South Point remain unverified via an allowlisted source.

location.region: Hawaii Island (Big Island), spreading impacts to Maui, Oahu and Kauai

event.scale: Weakened from Category 1 hurricane (75 mph, 15 August) to Tropical Storm (60 mph sustained winds, 16 August) as it moved away from the islands; NOAA forecasts possible re-strengthening to hurricane by 19 August
